title: flw review config
description: A reviewer team, as data. Shipped ones live in core/reviews/; a project's own in .flw/reviews/, which take precedence by name. The config says which lenses to look through; how to report and what to avoid is the skill's job and is not repeated per reviewer.

name.description: How the team is invoked. Matches the filename.

description.description: One line: what this team is for and when to reach for it.

reviewer.description: One entry per lens. Every reviewer is dispatched with the same instructions and a different perspective, so overlapping lenses produce overlapping findings and waste a context each.

question.description: One question every reviewer answers over its own zone, or over the whole scope when it has none. Stated once for the team rather than once per lens, so the lenses cannot drift on it.

shared.description: Optional. What every reviewer is asked in addition to its own question.

role.description: A short name for the lens. Appears in the consolidated report against every finding it produced.

model.description: Which class of model this lens runs on. Model names are host-specific; the agent doing the dispatching maps strong to the strongest thing it has, cheap to the cheapest, and inherit to whatever it is running on itself. Strong is for a question that needs tracing across files or a judgment a weaker read gets wrong silently; cheap is for a property checked mechanically or one zone read.

zone.description: Optional. The paths this reviewer reads, as a narrowing of the scope. Absent, the reviewer reads the whole scope. The orchestrator assigns none.

question.description: Optional. The one question only this lens answers, as a one-line form of perspective. A reviewer carries perspective or question; a config may give both, and then perspective is the long form.

probes.description: Whether this reviewer may execute things rather than only read — malformed input, boundary values, a re-run to check idempotency. Stated structurally rather than buried in the perspective, because an adversarial lane that is only ever described decays into opinion, and because it tells a reader which reviewers will run code.

perspective.description: What this lens looks for, and what it should leave to the others, in full. Written as instructions to the reviewer. Required unless question is given. Do not restate the reporting format or the general discipline — the skill supplies both to every reviewer, and repeating them here means they drift.
